messages.content: two groups of friends are having lunch at the park. one group wants soup and bread. the other wants rice and vegetables. do they have to choose the same meal?
not from what you said. they can choose different meals if they have a way to make or bring them. different food choices do not mean one group is wrong.
i am in the first group, and my sister is in the other. she says her meal is the best.
she may mean it is the meal she likes best. that is a choice about taste, not a fact that everyone must like the same food.
i like both choices, but soup is already ready at home.
then bringing soup could be the easiest choice for you today. you can still enjoy seeing your sister without having to choose her meal.
what if i say we should each bring what works for ourselves?
that sounds like a useful idea if the groups can both do that. you could also check whether anyone wants to share some of the food.
write that as one kind message.
we can each bring the meal that works for us. i will bring soup and bread, and you can bring rice and vegetables. we can still sit and enjoy lunch together.
what would you ask before making a list of food for everyone?
i would ask how many people are coming and what each person wants to bring.
what is the difference between who is by the door and whose book is by the door?
who is by the door asks about a person in that place. whose book is by the door asks which person the book is for or who has it as their own book.
the book is my cousin book. my cousin is a woman. i know that sentence about the book is not right. say it another way.
the book is hers.
use hers to answer the question about the book in a short sentence.
the book by the door is hers.
now give me a sentence with my cousin in it.
my cousin has a book by the door.
does that tell us she is standing by the door too?
no. her book can be by the door while she is in another place.
she is in the garden. what is the answer to who is by the door now?
you have not said that anyone is by the door. you said the book is there and your cousin is in the garden.
then answer whose book is by the door using only two words.
her book.
i put three pieces of fruit in a container this morning. now it is empty. does that tell you who took the fruit?
no. if the container is empty now, the fruit is no longer in it. that does not tell me who took it or what else happened to it.
my brother says somebody must have taken it to eat.
that is one possible explanation, but it is not the only one. the fruit could have been moved to another place. you would need more information to know whether anyone ate it.
i found two pieces on the kitchen table. how many of the original three are still not found?
one piece is still not found, if the two on the table are two of the original three.
why did you add if?
because finding two pieces of fruit does not by itself tell us they came from that container. i used your idea that they are the same pieces, but made that part of the answer clear.
i saw my sister take those two out of the container. she said she did not take the other one.
then you have information about the two on the table. you still do not know what happened to the other piece from what you have told me.
should i say she took all three?
no. that would add something you do not know from the information you gave.
my teacher explained a story to me, and i wrote down every word she wrote. does that mean i understood the story?
writing down the words is one thing. understanding the story is another. you could try saying what happened in your own words or answering a question about why someone did something.
she taught us that the boy in the story returned a book because it was not his. i can say that sentence back to her.
then try changing the words while keeping the reason. what could you say instead of it was not his?
he gave it back because the book was for someone else to keep.
that keeps the basic meaning. he returned the book because it was not his own to keep.
what if i say he returned it because he did not like reading?
that would change the reason. the first explanation was about whose book it was, not whether he liked reading.
can i ask my teacher to help me check my understanding without giving me the answer first?
yes. you could ask her to give you one question about the story and let you try answering before she gives you an explanation.
write that request in simple words.
could you ask me one question about the story and let me try before you explain the answer?
i can use one of two vehicles for a trip. the first can get me there in one hour. the other takes two hours, but it has more room for the things i need to bring. which is best?
what is most important for this trip? does the first vehicle have enough room for all your things, and do you need to get there in one hour?
the first one has enough room for all my things. i need the journey to take less than two hours.
then the first vehicle sounds like the useful choice from the details you gave. it has enough room and takes one hour. the other takes two hours, which would not get you there before that time.
can you say the first is always better?
no. on another trip, more room might be important. your answer today comes from this trip and the information you gave.
what do you know about the price?
you have not told me the price of either choice. i do not have information about that part yet.
i have enough money for either one. give me one short answer for today.
choose the first vehicle for this trip: it has enough room and gets you there before the time you gave.
the door closed by itself while i was reading. my friend says that must mean someone came into the room.
not always. a door closing does not by itself tell us that someone came in. do you have any other information, such as seeing a person or hearing a voice?
no. i only heard the door and then looked up. there was nobody else in the room.
then the information you have does not show that another person came into the room. you can say what you heard and saw without adding a person you did not see.
give me a shorter answer about that.
you heard the door close and then saw nobody else in the room. that does not tell us someone came in.
would it be okay to write a story where somebody came in quietly?
yes. that can be a story idea. just keep it apart from what you know happened in the real room.
what could i write in a note about the real thing?
i heard the door close while i was reading. when i looked up, i did not see anyone else in the room.
does the note tell us why the door closed?
no. it does not give a reason for the door closing, because you do not know that reason from what you saw and heard.
i have been watching two plants by my window. one is growing fast, and the other is growing slowly. should i say the slow one will never get large?
no. growing slowly now does not tell you that it will never get large. you would need more information about the kind of plant and how it is growing over time.
i only want to write what i have seen. help me make a clear sentence.
one plant by my window is growing fast, while the other is growing slowly.
can i add that the first one is better?
that would add your own choice about the plants, rather than only what you saw. you could say you enjoy watching the plant that is growing fast, but that is about your feeling.
how could i say that part about my feeling clearly?
you could say: i enjoy watching the plant that is growing fast. that says how you feel without making a rule about which plant is better.
i want to leave my feelings out too.
then keep only the sentence about what you saw: one plant is growing fast, while the other is growing slowly.
what should i check tomorrow if i want to know more?
you could look again and write down what has changed. keep the new note about what you can really see.
my aunt and uncle bought a small table. my brother helped carry it, and then i put a book on it. whose table is it?
it is the table your aunt and uncle bought. it does not become yours or the table your brother has to keep just because he carried it and you put a book on it.
use theirs to answer in a short sentence.
the table is theirs.
who does theirs mean here?
your aunt and uncle.
if my brother says our table while talking to me, is that the same meaning?
not in this conversation. our table could mean a table that is his and yours together. that is different from the table your aunt and uncle bought for themselves.
can i say our book if my brother and i own the book together?
yes. if the book is yours and his together, you can call it our book when you are talking about the two of you.
write one sentence that makes clear the table is theirs and the book is for my brother and me.
the table is theirs, and my brother and i own the book together.
what information made the last part possible?
you said you and your brother own the book together.
tell a story about someone who visits a village where she once lived. keep the story about places and her memory of them, not about buying things.

a woman returned to a village where she had lived as a child. she walked slowly along the road to her old house. the house had a different door now, but the tree in front was still there. she remembered sitting under it with her sister on warm days. she did not go inside the house, because other people lived there now. instead, she sat for a while by the road and wrote a few lines to her sister. she wrote that some things had changed and some things still helped her remember. before leaving, she looked at the tree once more and quietly said goodbye.
why did she not go inside?
other people lived in the house now. the story does not say she had been asked to come inside.
did the new door make what she remembered wrong?
no. the door had changed after she lived there. that did not make what she remembered about the old door or the tree wrong.
what was still there from when she was a child?
the tree in front of the house.
give me that answer in a full sentence.
the tree was still there from when she was a child.
what did she write to her sister?
she wrote that some things had changed and some things still helped her remember.
i found a pair of tools and one book by the door. how many objects is that?
a pair of tools is two tools. one book is one more object. that makes three objects.
one tool is red and the other is blue. does that change the number of objects?
no. a difference in color does not change how many objects are there. you still have two tools and one book.
if i put both tools into a container, is there now only one object in the whole story?
no. the container can hold the two tools, but that does not make them stop being two objects. the container is one object, and there are two more objects inside it.
what if i only ask how many things i need to carry, with the book in my other hand?
then you might mean the full container as one thing to carry and the book as another. i should ask what you want to count, rather than think it is the same question.
give me a clear question that asks about what is inside the container.
how many tools are inside the container?
and the answer?
two tools.
what was the useful difference between my questions?
one question was about each object, and another was about the things you would carry together.
i need to write a note, make tea, and leave for the library. the note is for my father, who will come home before i get back. help me choose the order and give the reasons.
write the note first so it is ready for your father. then make tea if you have enough time before leaving. put the note where he will see it before you go to the library.
why not make tea first?
you could, but the note is the part someone else will need while you are away. if you write it first, it will be ready even if you have to leave soon.
why did you say the note is for someone else?
you said the note was for your father, who will come home before you get back.
so it should be ready before i go?
yes. that gives your father the information while you are away. making tea can wait until the note is ready.
now give me only the order, without the reasons.
write the note, make tea if there is time, put the note where your father will see it, and leave for the library.
if there is no time for tea, is the whole plan impossible?
no. the plan already says to make tea only if there is time. the note and the library visit can still happen.
i need a solution for my kitchen table. it is not working for me.
what is the problem with it? is it too small, hard to use, or in the wrong place?
it is large enough. i keep putting books on it, so there is no clear place for meals.
then the problem seems to be what is on the table, rather than its size. do you have a place where the books could go before a meal?
there is an empty shelf near the door. i could use that.
that sounds like a useful solution to try. move the books to the shelf before meals and leave part of the table clear for food.
should i buy a larger table instead?
a larger table might just give you more room for books if the same thing keeps happening. from what you said, trying the empty shelf first would let you test a simple change without buying anything.
can you say that in a shorter way?
try using the empty shelf for books before buying another table. your table already has enough room when it is clear.
what did you ask before giving a solution?
i asked what was wrong with the table. your first message did not say what problem you wanted help with.

i have three messages from my friend. first she wrote that we should meet at my house. then she wrote that she would bring lunch. last she wrote that her sister would come too, if that was okay with me. how many people are coming?
your friend is coming, and she asked whether her sister could come too. her sister may come, but your friend is still waiting for your answer about that.
give the answer in a shorter way.
your friend is coming. her sister may come too, but your friend is waiting to know whether that is okay with you.
i said yes to her sister coming. what is the plan now?
your friend and her sister are coming to your house, and your friend said she would bring lunch.
does her sister have to bring another meal?
you have not said that. your friend said she would bring lunch, but there is no message saying the sister should bring another meal.
write one reply that says both can come and asks what i should have ready.
i would be happy to see both of you. thank you for bringing lunch. is there anything you would like me to have ready?
what changed after i said yes?
the sister coming is now part of the plan, rather than a question still waiting for your answer.
in this story, my cousin has a red vehicle. help me write one sentence about him going to the park.
my cousin went to the park on his red vehicle.
now we are starting a different story about my sister. she is walking to school. does she have the same red vehicle?
not from what you said. the red vehicle was part of the first story about your cousin. you have not given your sister a vehicle in this new story.
can both conversations use the word park without being the same story?
yes. different conversations can use the same word without having all the same people and facts.
i want a park in the story about my sister. write one sentence with her still walking.
my sister walked past the park on her way to school.
why did you not make her ride the vehicle?
because you said she was walking. bringing the vehicle from the first story into this one would add something you did not ask for.
what if i now tell you the cousin gave her the vehicle?
then that is new information you can add to the story. i would still need to know whether she will use it on this journey or keep walking.
just keep her walking for now.
she walked past the park on her way to school.
i want to take a trip next month. ask me the best first question to help make a plan.
where would you like to go?
i do not know yet. i only know that i want to visit a place i can reach and return from in one day.
then what kind of day would you enjoy: seeing a friend, walking outside, or visiting a new town?
a quiet walk outside, with time to have lunch before coming home.
that gives the plan a more clear goal. what places near your home could give you that kind of walk without a long journey?
there is a village near a park, and a city with a large market. i would rather not go where there are many people.
from those choices, the village near the park may work better for a quiet walk. i do not know how busy either place will be, so you would still need to check.
make that answer shorter.
from those choices, the village near the park may work better for a quiet walk. you should still check how many people are usually there.
what did the questions help us learn?
that you want a one day trip with a quiet walk and lunch, rather than just any new place.
write about two friends teaching each other something. neither should be better at everything.

two friends met at a table in the library. one liked drawing and knew how to make a house look clear on paper. the other liked writing and could put ideas into a simple order. first, they worked on a picture. the friend who liked drawing showed how to start with the large parts before adding small details. then they wrote a story about the house. the friend who liked writing asked what happened first and helped put the sentences in order. by the end, they had a picture and a story they had made together. each had taught something and learned something.
which friend was better at everything?
neither. they had different things to teach each other.
can i say they did it all themselves?
yes. the story says they made the picture and story together. it does not say someone else did the work for them.
does themselves mean just one of the two friends?
no. here, themselves is about both friends. each took part in the work.
write a sentence using ourselves as if the friends are talking together.
we made the picture and story ourselves.
what does adding details mean in the picture part?
you start with the large parts, then put the smaller parts into the picture.
i want to learn to draw, but i keep trying to work fast. then i feel sad when the picture is not clear.
you could try making the first goal smaller. choose one object and draw it slowly, looking at its large parts before adding more detail.
give me just the small first step.
choose one object and take your time. look at the large parts first, then add smaller details.
i think taking more time must mean i am not good at it.
taking more time can help you see more clearly and choose what to do next. being fast is only one part of doing something.
could taking more time make the picture better?
it could help if you use that time to look at the object and make your lines clear. more time by itself does not always make a better picture, but it can give you more room to think.
say the important part in a short way.
taking more time can help you see the object clearly. being fast is not the only way to do something well.
what could i say to myself before starting?
i can take my time and work on one part at a time.
keep that as the last answer, with no other information.
i can take my time and work on one part at a time.
in a photo, my brother seems to be holding a large fish. can you tell whether he bought it at the market?
not from those words alone. a photo of him holding a fish would not tell us how he got it or where he bought it.
he told me he did buy it at the market. does that change the answer?
it gives you information from what he said, as well as what is in the photo. you can say your brother told you he bought the fish at the market.
what if i want to write only about the fish in his hand, with no information about where he got it?
then write about what can be seen in the photo, without adding how the fish got there.
give me that sentence.
my brother is holding a large fish in the photo.
is it a problem that i first said seems?
seems can show that you are not sure what you are seeing. if the photo is not clear, you could keep that part of the meaning in the sentence.
use only the words we have and write the sentence with seems.
my brother seems to be holding a large fish in the photo.
so should you change seems to is every time?
no. changing it can make the answer sound as if the person is more sure of what they see. that can change the meaning.
i want to say two things together. the house is small. however, it has enough room for our family. is that a clear meaning?
yes. you are saying the house is small, while also saying that its size is enough for your family.
can you say it without however?
the house is small, but it has enough room for our family.
does that mean every small house has enough room for every family?
no. your sentence is about one house and your family. it does not make a rule about every house and every family.
i also want to say that we do not need to move now. add that without making it sound as if we can never move.
the house is small, but it has enough room for our family, so we do not need to move now.
why is now important?
it keeps the meaning about today. you can have enough room now and make a different choice later.
could our family need more room another year?
yes, that is possible. having enough room now does not tell us that you will always need the same space.
give me just the sentence with however again.
the house is small. however, it has enough room for our family, so we do not need to move now.
nobody in our family knows who opened the window. does that mean nobody opened it?
no. not knowing who did something is different from knowing that nobody did it. the window could have been opened even if no one can remember who did it.
i know it was closed before breakfast and open after lunch.
then you know something changed after breakfast and before lunch. you still do not know who changed it from that information alone.
say that in a more simple way.
it was closed before breakfast and open after lunch. something changed, but those facts do not tell us who opened it.
my sister said she might have opened it but cannot remember clearly.
then you have a possible explanation from her, rather than a clear answer that she knows she did it. you can keep that difference in how you tell the story.
write one sentence about what is known, without saying my sister is sure she did it.
the window was closed before breakfast and open after lunch, and my sister thinks she may have opened it.
should you leave out may have to make it shorter?
no. those words keep the part about her not being sure. taking them out would change the meaning.
my brother left a note that says i have gone to the park. does that mean he is sitting in the park right now?
it says he left to go to the park. it does not tell you where he is at this moment. he could still be on the way if he left only a short time before you read the note.
use only the words we have and say that more simply.
he left to go to the park, but the note does not tell you whether he has got there yet.
he left one minute before i read the note, and the walk takes ten minutes.
then he probably has not got there yet, if he is walking and the journey takes ten minutes as you said.
can i change the note to i am home because the park is near our house?
no. being near home is not the same as being at home. that would change the meaning of his note.
he has now returned and is in the kitchen. is he still gone?
no. in this conversation, he has come back. you can say he went to the park and then returned home.
write a short sentence about the whole trip, using gone first.
he had gone to the park, but he has now returned home.
make a short story with turned in it. i want the word to be about a person moving, not about changing the color of something.

a girl was reading at the kitchen table when she heard her father call from the garden. she turned to look through the window. he was holding a flower and wanted to show her its color. she was happy to see it, so she put her book down and went to the door. they talked for a while before she returned to her chair and began reading again.
give me only the part about what made her happy and what she did next.
she was happy to see the flower, so she put her book down and went to the door.
did turning to look through the window mean she was already in the garden?
no. she was still at the table when she turned to look. she went to the door after putting her book down.
what did she do when the conversation finished?
she returned to her chair and began reading again.
now ask me a short question about what happened when they finished talking.
what did she do when the conversation finished?
she returned to her chair. now give me only the sentence with turned.
she turned to look through the window.
